seven_q.Q0_posture: This document takes a structural-analytical posture, treating both epidemiology and theology as domains with shared mathematical dynamics.
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record mapping the SIR model of infectious disease to the propagation of sin in communities.
seven_q.Q2_domain: Lives at the intersection of epidemiology, mathematics, and Christian theology (hamartiology).
seven_q.Q3_claim: Sin spreads through communities according to the same mathematical structure as infectious disease: dS/dt = -βSI, dI/dt = βSI - γI, dR/dt = γI, with R₀ = β/γ determining whether sin becomes epidemic or is contained.
seven_q.Q4_support: Supported by 10 independent correspondences (R₀ threshold, transmission rate, recovery rate, herd immunity, super-spreaders, quarantine, contact tracing, asymptomatic carriers, vaccination, epidemic curves), biblical citations using contagion language, and empirical social network studies.
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: Depends on the SIR model from epidemiology, the concept of original sin from theology, and the general framework of structural isomorphisms.
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces that purely individualistic sanctification models will fail when R₀ > 1; requires community-level strategies (discipline, discipleship) to reduce transmission and increase recovery.
seven_q.Q7_kill: Would be falsified if sinful behaviors do not spread through social contact (zero social transmission), if church discipline has no effect on behavioral spread, or if spiritual herd immunity does not exist.

graph_summary.one_sentence: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between the SIR model of infectious disease and the propagation of sin in communities, showing that sin spreads according to the same mathematical dynamics as epidemics.
